title: Cohomology vanishes above the dimension of the support
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $\mathcal F$ be an abelian sheaf on the underlying topological space of $X$, and suppose that the support $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x\in X:\mathcal F_x\neq0\}$ (stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]) is contained in a closed subset $Z\subseteq X$ of topological Krull dimension at most $r$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], where $r\geq0$ is an integer. Then $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every integer $p>r$, with cohomology as in [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology].

source.place: Proposition 02UZ (cohomology-proposition-vanishing-Noetherian), applied to the closed support and Lemma 02UV (cohomology-lemma-cohomology-and-closed-immersions)

proof.text: Let i:Z\to X be the inclusion of the closed subset Z and consider the adjunction unit F\to i_*i^{-1}F. It is an isomorphism on stalks, hence an isomorphism of abelian sheaves: at x\notin Z both stalks are 0 (F_x=0 because Supp(F)\subseteq Z, and (i_*G)_x=0 since x has a neighbourhood missing Z), and at z\in Z the stalk of i_*i^{-1}F is (i^{-1}F)_z=F_z (Stacks 00AE). So F\cong i_*i^{-1}F.

source.place: Lemma 00AE and the stalkwise support argument

proof.text: The underlying space of the Noetherian scheme X is a Noetherian topological space [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. Hence the closed subspace Z is Noetherian: a nonempty set of closed subsets of Z is a nonempty set of closed subsets of X (Z being closed), so it has a minimal element (Stacks 0051; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace.set). Its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is at most r by hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 02UZ, applied to the closed subspace Z

proof.text: Apply the Noetherian topological cohomology vanishing theorem [lem-sc-noetherian-topological-cohomology-vanishing] to the abelian sheaf i^{-1}F on Z and the integer r. It gives H^p(Z,i^{-1}F)=0 for every p>r.

The closed-immersion cohomology comparison [lem-sc-cohomology-closed-immersion-pushforward] identifies H^p(Z,i^{-1}F) with H^p(X,i_*i^{-1}F), and the isomorphism from Step 1 identifies the latter with H^p(X,F). Therefore H^p(X,F)=0 for every p>r.
